info.title: SoroBeacon API
info.description:
Monitoring and alerting for Stellar/Soroban contract events. All endpoints are mounted under /api/v1. The API is read-write for monitors, rules and channels; alerts are read-only.

Authentication: when API_TOKEN is configured, every endpoint below requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and answers 401 through the standard error envelope without one. The only exceptions are the probes /livez, /readyz and /health, which stay reachable so an orchestrator does not need the token. With API_TOKEN unset the API is open and none of this applies.

post.description: Sets enabled on an explicit list of monitor IDs in one statement. Unknown IDs are returned and do not prevent the known ones from applying. There is no all-monitors shorthand.

post.summary: Create several rules in one request
post.description: Validates every rule first, then inserts the batch in a single transaction. An empty array is 400. At most 50 rules per request.

get.description: Alert, delivery and per-rule counts for one monitor — the answer to "is this monitor doing anything", which the instance-wide /stats cannot give. Counts are explicit zeroes for a monitor with no history, and every one of the monitor's rules appears with its own alert count, including rules that never matched. An unknown monitor is 404 rather than a body of zeroes, so a deleted monitor cannot be misread as a quiet one.

post.description: Copies the monitor with its rules and channel attachments under a unique name. The copy is created disabled so it cannot start alerting before review. Alerts are not copied.

get.description: Returns the ordered escalation steps attached to the monitor. 404 when the monitor has no policy, in which case alerts fan out to every attached channel.

put.summary: Create or replace a monitor's escalation policy
put.description: Replaces the whole policy atomically. Steps fire in order; a step's delay is relative to the alert for the first step and to the previous step thereafter. An unknown channel id is 400.

delete.description: Removes the policy so the monitor fans out flat again. 404 when the monitor has no policy.

post.summary: Dry-run a rule against historical events
post.description: Evaluates a candidate rule against stored alert history. Nothing is persisted and nothing is delivered. Stored alerts are biased toward matched events, so results underrepresent the true event corpus.

get.summary: Stream alerts as they are created (Server-Sent Events)
get.description: Opens a text/event-stream response that emits an `alert` event for every alert created after the connection opened. SSE rather than WebSockets: the traffic is one-directional and SSE reconnects on its own. An optional monitor_id filters server-side. Comment lines (keep-alives) are sent periodically so idle connections are not reaped by a proxy, and the stream advertises a 3000ms retry hint. A subscriber that cannot keep up loses its oldest queued events rather than blocking alert creation.

parameters.name: monitor_id
parameters.description: Only stream alerts created by this monitor

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream; each `alert` event's data is one alert object

get.description: Streams every alert matching the same filters as GET /alerts as text/csv. Columns are fixed: id, monitor_name, rule_id, contract_id, event_name, event_id, ledger, created_at, payload, network. Column position is part of the contract, so a new column is always appended, never inserted. Values beginning with =, +, - or @ are prefixed with an apostrophe to prevent spreadsheet formula injection. When no limit is given the export is capped at 10000 rows.

post.description: Records a new delivery attempt for one alert and channel. Rejects a channel that already succeeded (409), a disabled channel (400), a missing prior attempt (404), and repeats inside a 30s cooldown (429). Synchronous: the response is the new attempt.

post.summary: Receive a federated alert from another SoroBeacon instance
post.description: Stores an alert forwarded by another instance without re-evaluating rules. The alert is stamped with its origin and hop count for loop prevention. Requires authentication.

origin.description: Instance identifier of the originating SoroBeacon

hop_count.description: Number of hops this alert has traversed

get.description: Legacy combined check; prefer /livez and /readyz. Exempt from authentication so probes and the docker-compose healthcheck keep working. Reports `leader` (whether this instance holds the poller lease), `leader_election` (whether a lease exists to hold at all; false for a single-node/ SQLite deployment) and `leader_since`. A follower is healthy: it serves the API and dashboard and returns 200.

Legacy combined check; prefer /livez and /readyz. Exempt from authentication so probes and the docker-compose healthcheck keep working. On an instance that polls several Stellar networks the body adds a `networks` array — per chain: source state, last processed ledger, chain tip, lag and last successful poll — and answers 503 `degraded` when any chain's source is failing. The top-level `rpc` field is only ever the primary chain's source, which is why the array exists.
Answers 200 whenever the process can respond; checks no dependencies. Wire to livenessProbe. Exempt from authentication.

Checks the database and the event source concurrently, bounded by a 3s timeout each, reporting per-dependency detail. On an instance that polls several Stellar networks each chain gets its own check (`rpc_testnet`, `rpc_mainnet`, ...) alongside the primary chain's `rpc`, so a node that is down on one chain cannot read as ready. Wire to readinessProbe. Exempt from authentication, so its per-dependency detail is readable without a token — do not expose it to the public internet.

Reports the last successful poll position, chain tip, ledger lag, and whether the poller is currently backing off. Before the first successful poll, position fields are omitted and status is waiting. No configuration values are returned.

parameters.name: name

post.description:
Creates a database-backed credential: `sb_` followed by 32 random bytes, base64url-encoded. The response's `token` field is the only place the secret ever appears — the row stores a SHA-256 digest of it, so it cannot be read back, listed, logged or recovered. A client that loses the secret mints a new token and revokes the old one.

`scopes` is required and non-empty: a token with no scope authenticates and can then call nothing. Every scope must come from the enumeration below. A request carrying a scoped token may only grant scopes it already holds, so `tokens:write` is not a road back to full control. `expires_in` is a Go duration string (`72h`, `168h`); omit it for a token that never expires.

201.description: Minted. The only response in the API that contains a token secret.

get.description: Lists the caller's workspace's tokens: name, display prefix, scopes and lifecycle timestamps. Never a secret and never the stored digest.

post.description: Stops a token immediately: the next request with it authenticates as no credential at all. The row survives with its `revoked_at` set, so the audit trail (name, prefix, scopes, last use) outlives the credential. Revoking twice is idempotent and keeps the first `revoked_at`. A token can only be revoked by the workspace that owns it; another workspace's id and a nonexistent id get the same 404.

bearerAuth.description: Any of three credentials. (1) A static token from API_TOKEN (comma-separated to allow rotation): full reach over the default workspace. (2) A scoped token minted by POST /tokens — it looks like `sb_…`, and carries a scope list, an optional expiry and a revocation. Each route names the scopes it requires; a route that has no mapping denies a scoped token with 403 rather than allowing it. (3) A dashboard session cookie from /login, accepted in the browser's own same-origin requests. A token from WORKSPACE_TOKENS (`workspace=token` pairs) is accepted the same way as (1) but additionally scopes the request: it sees and changes only that workspace's monitors, channels, rules, alerts, saved searches and templates. `API_TOKEN`'s tokens belong to the `default` workspace, as do rows created before workspaces existed. Scoped tokens are workspace-bound too: the workspace comes from the row that stores the token's digest, not from the request. There is deliberately no X-Workspace header or query parameter — the workspace is a property of the credential, so a client cannot ask for another tenant's data.

TokenManagementDisabled.description: Token management is not configured on this instance: it needs a database-backed store, so an unset deployment answers this way rather than pretending to mint.

code.description: Stable status token, e.g. Not Found

request_id.description: Correlation ID, also on the X-Request-ID response header

details.description: Field-level validation problems. Omitted when there are none so existing clients keep working. Each entry names a JSON path and why it failed; all problems in one request are listed together.

field.description: Dotted JSON path of the offending field, e.g. rules[0].params.min_amount

network.description: Stellar chain this monitor watches. Empty on rows created before multi-network ingestion, which startup labels with the primary network.

last_alert_at.description: Absent when the monitor has never alerted

rules.description: Every rule of the monitor, matched or not

network.description: Stellar chain these contract ids live on, chosen at creation. Omitted means the instance's primary network (the first entry in NETWORKS, or NETWORK when unset). A name this instance does not poll is rejected: the monitor would match nothing forever. A monitor's network cannot be changed afterwards — a contract id resolves to a different contract on another chain, and the alerts already stored keep their old label — so moving one means deleting and recreating it.

updated.description: How many existing monitors changed state

firing_window_seconds.description: Source counts as firing with an alert inside this window
Optional; defaults to 300 when absent or non-positive

params.description: Type-specific; validated against the rule type

timeout.description: HTTP delivery timeout in seconds (default: 15, range 1-60)

consecutive_failures.description: Deliveries that have failed since the last success. One success resets it to 0.

consecutive_permanent_failures.description: Permanent failures (401/403/404) since the last success. This is what auto-disable counts; a transient 5xx or timeout neither increments nor clears it.

last_error.description: Most recent failure message, empty once a delivery succeeds. Never contains channel config.

last_error_at.description: When last_error was recorded. Absent if there has been no failure since the last success.

last_success_at.description: Last delivery that succeeded. Absent until the first one.

disabled_at.description: Set when health tracking auto-disabled the channel, absent when it is on or an operator disabled it. Cleared only by explicitly re-enabling the channel.

config.description: Type-specific; the channel reference documents each

digest_mode.description: Empty delivers immediately; window batches into one summary per digest_window_seconds

digest_window_seconds.description: Accumulation window when digest_mode is window; must be > 0 then

timeout.description: HTTP delivery timeout in seconds (default: 15, range 1-60)

network.description: Stellar chain the matching event came from. Taken from the monitor, never from the caller: it is what a reorg on that chain may retract and no other chain's.

suppressed.description: True when a maintenance window silenced delivery

end_at.description: Must be after start_at; open-ended windows are rejected

delay.description: Go duration before this step fires, e.g. 5m

steps.description: Ordered escalation steps. The first fires immediately; each later step waits its delay after the previous one fired.

delay.description: Go duration, e.g. 5m. Omitted or empty fires immediately.

network.description: Chain the instantiated monitor watches. A template is chain-agnostic text, so this defaults to the instance's primary network.

Chain every monitor in this batch watches. Omitted means the primary. The already-monitored check is per network: the same id on another chain is a different contract, and watching it there is normal.

count.description: Number of historical events that matched the rule

total_evaluated.description: Total number of historical events evaluated
